title: Development of the Self-Perceived Capability for Human–AI Collaborative Spoken English Learning Scale and Its Preliminary Application Among Secondary School Students
abstract: Grounded in Bem’s self-perception theory and the AIEd Bloom’s taxonomy model, this study developed the Self-Perceived Capability for Human–AI Collaborative Spoken English Learning scale, following the procedure of theory-based construction, item generation, scale validation, and preliminary application. From an initial pool of 36 items, expert review, cognitive interviews, item analysis, exploratory factor analysis, and confirmatory factor analysis yielded a 30-item scale covering four dimensions: Acquisition and Adjustment, Scenario Simulation, Analysis and Diagnosis, and Evaluation and Creation. A preliminary application among secondary school students showed that their capability was overall moderate and clearly differentiated by activity type: Scenario Simulation was strongest, Analysis and Diagnosis and Acquisition and Adjustment were intermediate, and Evaluation and Creation was weakest. Students with longer cumulative duration of AI use scored significantly higher than those with shorter duration on all four dimensions, and three learner profiles were identified: the Well-Balanced Type, the Simulation-Dominant Type, and the Overall Developing Type. The scale demonstrated good construct validity and reliability; it can be used to diagnose learners’ level and capability profile for human–AI collaborative spoken English learning and to inform differentiated instruction and targeted intervention.
